messages:
maria: Quick thread — noticed a few folks hit onboarding friction w/ key discovery and rotation in the SDKs today. Can we align on a pragmatic priority order for creds and a UX for rotation?
aj: yep saw the error reports. mostly 401s without actionable text. users don't know whether key expired, scoped incorrectly, or wrong org. :grimacing:
soren: Current priority in most SDKs is: env var -> config file -> explicit param. But env var names vary across languages (REDWOOD_API_KEY, RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_KEY). That inconsistency is driving help-desk noise.
maria: Proposal: standardize on 2 env vars across all SDKs: REDWOOD_API_KEY (primary) and RW_SESSION (short-lived refresh token). SDKs should accept legacy names with a deprecation warning at runtime.
olivia: +1. How do we surface the deprecation warning without being too noisy for infra users? Maybe log one warning per process and include a link to migration docs.
aj: For rotation UX thought: expose a refresh hook in each SDK that apps can register. On 401, SDK tries one refresh attempt (if RW_SESSION present) then falls back to failing with a structured error containing: code, retryable boolean, suggested action, and a docs link.
soren: example structured error idea: 
```
{
  "code": "auth.invalid_key",
  "http": 401,
  "retryable": false,
  "action": "rotate_api_key",
  "help_url": "https://redwood.dev/docs/auth/errors#auth.invalid_key"
}
```
This makes it easy for app teams to map errors to product UX.
mar ia: tiny nit: prefer snake_case keys for consistency with other SDK errors (we already use that elsewhere).
aj: also suggest SDKs print a short one-line hint when they detect org/project mismatch in request meta — e.g., "request org=acme-corp but key scopes: org=acme-dev; consider using REDWOOD_ORG or request-scoped key". That helped one customer debug in 3 mins earlier.
soren: for key discovery priority, suggest this exact order: 1) explicit param to client constructor, 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, 3) ~/.redwood/credentials, 4) platform-injected metadata (CI secrets). Accept legacy names but emit deprecation logs.
olivia: We should also document secret rotation guidance for Dedicated/Private customers: prefer short-lived credentials + automated CI job to rotate and push new secret, and provide a small helper CLI command `rw auth rotate --service <name>` that updates env secret store and prints sample diff.
sam: ops ask: what about automatic retries while rotating? We shouldn't silently retry on 401s without a refresh attempt — it masks failures. So SDK should only retry idempotent requests after successful token refresh; otherwise bubble up.
maria: Good constraint. Add exponential backoff cap for retry attempts (2 tries max).
dev-bot: Deploy note: added a ticket INF-3217 to standardize env var names across SDKs and INF-3218 for structured error spec.
aj: UX for console: when CLI sees a near-expiry key (expires within 48h) it should prompt: "Detected API key expiring in 36h. Rotate now? (y/N)" and include a link to `rw auth rotate` docs. Non-interactive CI should accept `--auto-rotate`.
soren: For sample apps, include a tiny snippet showing refresh hook: 
```
client.on('auth:refresh', async (ctx) => {
  // exchange RW_SESSION for new key
  const newKey = await fetchToken(ctx.session);
  client.setKey(newKey);
});
```
This clarifies integration points.
olivia: logging: when we emit a deprecation warning for env var name, include the detected location (env/config file) and the recommended var. Example: "DEPRECATED: found REDWOOD_KEY in env; use REDWOOD_API_KEY. See https://redwood.dev/migrate-keys"
maria: Ok next steps: aj and soren to draft the structured error JSON schema, olivia to draft the deprecation wording and CLI prompt wording, sam to validate retry rules with SRE. I'll collate into a single PR for SDKs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
aj: I'll ping when PRs are up.
sam: Will check the SRE playbook for impacts.
olivia: I'll add a mini sample app demonstrating rotation and RW_SESSION exchange.
mar ia: Thanks — small changes but should cut onboarding tickets a lot. :party_parrot:
